02 · The Diagnostic

Strategic Assessment

BCG's outside-in view on NAC — non-exhaustive

The NAC currently has assets most new cities spend decades building...

The NAC currently has assets most new cities spend decades building

Government & embassy anchoring demand

Ministries, public authorities and planned embassy presence create a permanent institutional base, bringing daily footfall and credibility to the city.

SOE ecosystem

State-owned enterprises, banks and major public entities create a second layer of demand, supporting employee movement and NAC footfall.

Infrastructure-led connectivity

The NAC is being connected through major road networks, monorail, high-speed rail and an airport, making it increasingly accessible from Greater Cairo and key national destinations.

Emerging incentive framework

Potentially providing a unique edge to attract private sector businesses from within and beyond Egypt's business ecosystem.

...but critical constraints need to be addressed to enable full city activation

What stands between today's footprint and tomorrow's city

Competing local mega-projects

Multiple local mega-projects are also competing for investor attention and residents, making NAC's positioning increasingly important.

Slower residential uptake

Residential uptake is taking time as affordability, services, and lifestyle amenities continue to mature.

Potential private-sector lag

A lack of visible private-sector relocation at scale exists, as companies are awaiting clear proof of incentives and market demand.

Perception gap

Perception of limited activity may persist unless matched with stronger activation, communications, and visible success stories.

04 · The Framework

Successful city activation hinges on two interconnected fronts

Economic activation and livability are the two critical fronts that convert infrastructure into demand, daily activity, and long-term commitment.

Key strategic questions for the NAC's next phase are organized across two fronts: economic activation and livability.

Pillar 01

Economic Activation

Build a self-sustaining productive economy.

Areas to Explore
  • How can NAC use the critical mass of government-driven footfall to activate livability anchors and generate economic activity?
  • How can government-driven footfall be translated into demand for retail, F&B, services, entertainment, and other daily-use amenities?
Government relocation is the first demand engine — not the end state. The priority is converting institutional presence into livability anchors and daily-use demand that compound into broader economic activity.
Areas to Explore
  • Which private-sector industries should form the economic foundation of NAC?
  • Which players can act as anchor tenants and drive additional demand?
  • What is NAC's right to win in attracting specific sectors to the New Administrative Capital?
Anchor Example
For example, the relocation of state-owned banks could help establish a financial-services anchor and stimulate adjacent private-sector demand.
Priority Sectors
Financial institutions Tech & AI Hospitality Healthcare …
Pillar 02

Livability

Make the NAC a city people actively choose — and choose to stay in.

Areas to Explore
  • What is the bare minimum NAC needs to offer to be considered an attractive and livable city?
  • Where does it make sense for NAC to subsidize, promote, or directly support livability anchors?
  • What is the minimum viable livability proposition required for NAC to succeed?
  • Which activities, services, amenities, and supporting ecosystem components are required to create destination gravity?
The NAC needs reasons for people to come before they choose to live there. Destination gravity is built through activities, services, amenities, and a supporting ecosystem — including cultural programming, events, and education-led demand — that create visible activity and shift perception.
Areas to Explore
  • What elements need to be in place to create a credible livability proposition for residents?
  • How can usability and transportation improve the daily experience for residents, workers, and visitors?
  • Which world-class operators are needed across daily operations — including schools, hospitals, and services — before families commit?
  • Where does NAC need to invest to attract the right livability anchors, especially where supply may need to precede demand?
Reduce the opportunity cost of relocating by creating the right mix of livability, services, mobility, incentives, and private-sector opportunities — building the environment required for private-sector players, residents, and talent to commit to NAC rather than treat it as a commuter destination.
The Cycle

Economic activation and livability must advance together

Economic Activation

  • Anchor tenants & private-sector demand
  • Investment momentum & ecosystem build-out
  • Industry clusters and employment density
⇌

Livability

  • Residents, talent & daily-life amenities
  • Culture, retail, F&B & public realm
  • Mobility, services & quality of life

Each fuels the other — jobs and investment draw residents; vibrant residents and amenities deepen the economy. Neither stands alone.
